lead: A vector path is a list of anchor points joined by Bezier segments. The pen tool places an anchor; dragging before release pulls out handles. Those handles set the tangent, so the next segment leaves and arrives at the angle you want. Designers use paths for logos, icons, fonts and maps because the artwork is stored as geometry, not pixels. Only a few universities teach this chapter.
prereq: You need Unit 1 on raster versus vector graphics and Unit 3 on Bezier curves.

blocks.text: A path has three parts. An anchor point is a location on the path. A handle (control point) pulls the curve and is not on it. A segment is the curve between two anchors. Some syllabi call anchors nodes and handles direction lines. At a smooth point the two handles lie on one straight line, so the curve passes through without a kink. At a corner point they do not, so the path turns sharply. Dragging a handle after placing an anchor sets the tangent; clicking with no drag gives a straight corner. An open path has two ends; a closed path joins its last anchor to its first. Fill paints the inside; stroke paints the outline. Union, subtract and intersect combine two closed paths into a new path. Converting a path to a selection makes a marching-ants region; the path stays a separate object. The pen tool is the usual way to place these parts.
Each curved segment is a cubic Bezier with four points: anchors P₀ and P₃, handles P₁ and P₂. For 0 ≤ t ≤ 1,

blocks.where: B(t) is the point at parameter t. P₀ and P₃ are the start and end anchors. P₁ is the handle leaving P₀; P₂ is the handle arriving at P₃. Each term is a weight times a control point, and the four weights sum to 1.

blocks.text: To evaluate by de Casteljau, split P₀P₁, P₁P₂ and P₂P₃ at ratio t, join the three new points, split those two lines again, then split the last line once more; that point is B(t). Direct substitution gives the same answer. Differentiate: B′(0) = 3(P₁ − P₀). The tangent at t = 0 points along P₁ − P₀. Vector art scales because the file stores anchors, handles and fill rules as numbers. At any zoom the renderer recomputes the curve and paints fresh pixels. Nothing is enlarged, so no pixel blocks appear. A raster logo stretched to billboard size shows squares; the same logo as a path stays sharp. This is why fonts, icons and maps ship as paths. The trade-off is more computation at render time, not more storage.

figure.caption: The blue arch is the path from P₀(0, 0) to P₃(50, 0); the grey corner is the two handles, which the curve bends toward but never touches. It peaks at B(0.5) = (25, 37.5) mm, and the handle straight above P₀ makes the path leave vertically upward.

spec.aria: A plot of the cubic Bezier path in millimetres from anchor (0, 0) to anchor (50, 0), arching through its midpoint (25, 37.5), with the control polygon rising through handle (0, 50) and handle (50, 50) above it.

examples.question: A cubic Bezier has P₀(0, 0), P₁(0, 50), P₂(50, 50), P₃(50, 0), in millimetres. Find B(0.5) and the tangent direction at t = 0.
steps: B′(0) = 3(P₁ − P₀) = 3(0, 50) = (0, 150). The direction is +y, so it is vertical upward.
examples.answer: B(0.5) = (25, 37.5) mm; the tangent at the start has direction (0, 150), vertically upward.

traps: A handle pulls the curve, but the curve does not pass through it; only anchors lie on the path.
A path is not a selection. Converting a path to a selection creates a pixel-edge mask and leaves the path separate.
Smooth anchors have collinear handles; corner anchors do not.
The start tangent is 3(P₁ − P₀), not 3(P₀ − P₁); reversing the subtraction flips the arrow.

quiz.q: Define anchor point and handle in a path.
quiz.a: Anchor: a point on the path where segments meet. Handle: an off-curve control point that sets a segment's tangent and pull.

quiz.q: What does closing a path change?
quiz.a: It joins the last anchor to the first and lets the interior be filled.

quiz.q: Why does a smooth anchor avoid a visible kink?
quiz.a: Its two handles are collinear, so the incoming and outgoing tangents point along one line.

quiz.q: How is a path different from a selection?
quiz.a: A path stores editable geometry; a selection marks pixels and has no anchors.

quiz.q: A cubic has P₀(0,0), P₁(0,30), P₂(30,30), P₃(30,0). Find the tangent vector at t = 0.
quiz.a: B′(0) = 3(P₁ − P₀) = 3(0,30) = (0,90). It points vertically upward.

quiz.q: An artist drags a handle far from the curve, yet the curve does not touch it. Explain.
quiz.a: The handle is a control point, not a point on the path. The curve is a weighted average of all four points, so it bends toward the handle but passes only through anchors.

beyond: Not for the exam. SVG stores each path in a d attribute as move, line, cubic and close commands, so the same geometry drives web icons. Font editors build glyph outlines from cubic or quadratic Bezier paths. GIS and CAD tools use paths for roads and machine parts because scale independence matters. Search SVG path commands, font outline design, and Bezier handle editing.
